name: GPT-OSS 120B
notes: PARAMS: 116.8B is the safetensors weight count from the Hugging Face model metadata; OpenAI's card says 117B. Not contested, just rounding. ACTIVE: 5.1B is OpenAI's published figure, not derived. KV: 36 layers * 8 kv heads * 64 head_dim * 2 (K and V) * 2 bytes (bf16) = 73,728 bytes/token = 72 KiB/token. At 128k context that is about 9.0 GiB for one sequence. SLIDING WINDOW IS THE SERVING POINT: sliding_window=128 with alternating dense/locally-banded layers (OpenAI's wording) means only a small fraction of the layers attend over the whole 128k. A naive full-attention KV estimate overcharges by roughly 2x because every other layer keeps only a 128-token window. EXPERTS: 128 experts per layer, 4 routed per token, no shared expert. With hidden_size == intermediate_size == 2880 the per-expert FFN is small relative to attention, so MoE weight streaming dominates the memory profile: all 117B must be resident even though only 5.1B is active. MXFP4: the released MoE weights are MXFP4-quantized with bf16 attention/embedding tensors (HF metadata shows 114.7B U8-packed MXFP4 + 2.2B BF16). This is why the 120B fits on one 80GB device.
